History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
- 25-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presents via telehealth with a first-ever, 1-day history of left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia; clinical impression is probable migraine; advised trial of ibuprofen plus paracetamol, hydration, blood-pressure check, and red-flag precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint: New, severe headache.
- Onset: Began yesterday morning upon waking (≈24 h ago).
- Duration/progression: Continuous baseline pain that fluctuates in intensity; has not fully resolved.
- Location: Predominantly left side of head.
- Quality: Throbbing, “quite intense.”
- Exacerbating factors: Bright light/sunlight.
- Relieving factors: Lying down, dark environment, paracetamol (partial).
- Associated symptoms:
  • Photophobia.
  • Denies nausea, vomiting.
  • Denies visual disturbances, abnormal smells/tastes.
  • Denies fever (no thermometer available).
  • Denies weakness, numbness, tingling, or focal neurological deficit.
  • Denies cough, runny nose, sore ears, skin changes, rash.
- Prior history of headaches: None.
- Menstrual history: Last period ~1 week ago; no clear cyclical pattern noted.
- Current self-management: Paracetamol taken; has avoided aspirin due to allergy; no NSAIDs taken yet.
- Review of systems: Remainder negative as per above.

Past Medical History:
- No prior significant illnesses, hospitalizations, or surgeries reported.
- Contraception: Combined oral contraceptive pill (Microgynon) for 6 years; no noted side effects.
- Allergies: Aspirin – causes marked nausea.

Social History:
- Lives with friends/housemates.
- Occupation not specified; reports recent work-related stress.
- Alcohol: “A few drinks at the weekend.”
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
- Mother: Hypertension and history of migraines.
- No other familial conditions mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Teleconsultation; no in-person examination performed.
- Vitals: Not obtained.

Investigations:
- None performed during call.
- Advised to obtain blood-pressure check.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: New-onset left-sided throbbing headache, likely migraine without aura.
  - Start NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) in addition to ongoing paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Maintain good oral hydration.
  - Minimize light exposure; rest as needed.
  - Red-flag advice: Seek immediate review if headache worsens, changes character, persists, or if fever, rash, neurological symptoms, or other systemic features develop.
  - Arrange BP measurement soon (pharmacy, GP surgery).
  - Consider follow-up discussion if headaches recur, become cyclical, or are otherwise persistent to evaluate for migraine prophylaxis or alternate diagnoses.

- Issue 2: Aspirin allergy (nausea).
  - Avoid aspirin-containing products.
  - Document in records.

- Issue 3: Combined oral contraceptive use.
  - Continue current Microgynon; no side effects reported.
  - Monitor if migraine frequency increases; consider alternative contraception if migraine with aura develops.

General plan items:
- Obtain home thermometer for self-monitoring.
- Re-contact clinic if any concerns or questions arise.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Objective vitals, focused neurological and fundoscopic examination, medication reconciliation details (doses/frequencies), full allergy list beyond aspirin.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational fillers, no significant inaudible sections.
